quote: Blood gene expression analysis of an independent cohort, identified TREM-1 downregulation in non-responders at baseline, which was predictive of response with an AUC of 94%.
summary: Baseline blood TREM-1 was lower in anti-TNF non-responders with IBD and predicted response (AUC 94%); biopsy TREM-1 was higher in non-responders.

quote: TREM1 and CTGF were identified as two activated regulators associated with CRC aggressiveness.
summary: In colorectal cancer RNA-seq, TREM1 was inferred as an activated regulator linked to aggressiveness, and a signature of TREM1/CTGF-regulated genes was prognostic; this is not a UC study.

quote: Low TREM1 expression in whole blood predicts anti-TNF response in inflammatory bowel disease.
summary: Low baseline whole-blood TREM1 expression predicted anti-TNF endoscopic remission in UC and Crohn's patients, and was specific to anti-TNF therapy.

quote: TREM1 inhibition genetically or pharmacologically improved outcome via protective antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms.
summary: In mouse stroke, TREM1 inhibition improved outcome, and TREM1 induction on gut macrophages increased gut permeability; this is a stroke model, not colitis.

quote: We identified novel host biomarkers of pediatric severe and fatal malaria (soluble TREM-1 and soluble Flt-1) and generated simple biomarker combinations that accurately predicted death in an African pediatric population.
summary: Plasma soluble TREM-1 was a prognostic marker of death in children with severe malaria; not a UC study.

quote: In CD4(+) T cell- and dextran sodium sulfate-induced models of colitis, Trem1(-/-) mice displayed significantly attenuated disease that was associated with reduced inflammatory infiltrates and diminished expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
summary: Trem1 knockout mice had milder T cell-transfer and DSS colitis with less infiltration and cytokine expression, while still controlling infections.

quote: During a CD4(+) T-cell-induced colitis, CX3CR1(lo) cells accumulate in the inflamed mucosa and upregulate the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1 (TREM-1).
summary: In T-cell-induced mouse colitis, CX3CR1-low intestinal phagocytes accumulated in inflamed mucosa and upregulated TREM-1 along with pro-inflammatory cytokines.
The paper is about soluble TLT-1 (TREML1) in sepsis; TREM-1 appears only as the competing ligand target, with no result about TREM1 itself.

quote: According to experimental data, inhibiting macrophage migration inhibitory factor, high-mobility group box protein 1 (HMGB1), and complement factor C5a and inhibiting the TREM-1 (triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 1) signaling pathway and apoptosis represent promising new therapeutic options.
summary: A sepsis review focused on RAGE that lists TREM-1 pathway inhibition among several promising sepsis options, without detail on TREM1.

quote: Transcriptional profiling identifies markers that define the CD103+CD11b+ DC lineage, including CD101, TREM1 and Siglec-F, and shows that the absence of CD103+CD11b+ DCs in CD11c-Cre.Tgfbr1 fl/fl mice reflects defective differentiation from CD103-CD11b+ intermediaries, rather than an isolated loss of CD103 expression.
summary: TREM1 is named only as one of several marker genes of intestinal CD103+CD11b+ dendritic cells; the paper is about TGFbR1 signalling.

quote: Trem1-/-Apoe-/- mice exhibit substantially attenuated diet-induced atherogenesis.
summary: Trem1 deletion reduced diet-induced atherosclerosis and monocytosis in Apoe-null mice; this is an atherosclerosis model, not colitis.

quote: In this review, we highlight the emerging roles of TREM-1, including synergy with classical pathogen recognition receptors.
summary: Review of TREM-1 in antiviral immunity, noting its pathogenic or protective roles are unclear; no UC content.

quote: Conversely, immediately upon entry into the inflamed intestine, monocytes adapt a different expression pattern in a partly Trem-1-dependent manner.
summary: In mouse small-intestine inflammation, monocyte gene expression changes were partly Trem-1-dependent; no colitis severity outcome is given in the abstract.

quote: The TREM-1 peptides inhibited the recognition by TREM-1 of its ligand and protected endotoxinic mice from death.
summary: TREM-1 inhibitory peptides protected endotoxin-challenged mice and septic rats and lowered cytokines; this is sepsis, not colitis.

quote: Here we report on the potential usefulness of assessing the soluble form of TREM-1 (sTREM-1) in biological fluids for the diagnosis of microbial infection.
summary: Soluble TREM-1 in body fluids was assessed as a diagnostic marker of microbial infection and sepsis; not a UC study.

quote: TREM-1 multimerization at the cell surface is also mediated by its endogenous ligand, a conclusion supported by the ability of the TREM-1 inhibitor LR12 to limit TREM-1 multimerization.
summary: In human monocytes and neutrophils, TREM-1 activation and cytokine output depended on multimerization, which the inhibitor LR12 limited; no UC outcome was tested.

quote: Synovial TREM-1 expression is increased in septic arthritis and RA.
summary: TREM-1 was raised in synovial fluid and tissue of septic arthritis and rheumatoid arthritis patients; not a UC study.

quote: The inflammatory response mediated by Toll-like receptor-2 and -4 stimulation is amplified by the engagement of TREM-1.
summary: Clinical review of TREM-1 in sepsis covering its amplification of inflammation, soluble form as a marker, and peptide modulation; no UC content.

quote: Moreover, the TREM1 inhibitor weakened the effect of salidroside on BMDMs pyroptosis, whereas salidroside still could downregulate TREM1 when NLRP3 was inhibited.
summary: Salidroside lowered TREM1 in DSS colitis, and a TREM1 inhibitor weakened its anti-pyroptosis effect in macrophages; the direction of TREM1 itself is not clearly resolved.

quote: The disease is caused by mutations in the TYMP gene encoding thymidine phosphorylasethymine phosphorylase.
summary: Clinical and mutation spectrum of MNGIE, a rare recessive disease caused by TYMP mutations; it is not about UC.

quote: Mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy (MNGIE) is a rare autosomal recessive disease caused by TYMP mutations and thymidine phosphorylase (TP) deficiency.
summary: Consensus position paper on MNGIE diagnosis and treatment, caused by TYMP mutations; nothing on UC.

quote: In contrast to the heterogeneous CoQ(10) deficiencies, MNGIE is a single autosomal recessive disease due to mutations in the TYMP gene encoding thymidine phosphorylase (TP).
summary: Review of treatable mitochondrial disorders explaining how loss of TYMP activity causes toxic nucleoside accumulation in MNGIE; no UC content.

quote: Quantitative expression levels of drug pathway genes were determined using TaqMan RT-PCR (5-fluorouracil (5-FU): TYMS, DPYD, ECGF1; oxaliplatin: GSTP1 (glutathione S-transferase pi), ERCC1 and 2; irinotecan: ABCB1, ABCG2, CYP3A4, UGT1A1, CES2, TOP1).
summary: ECGF1 (TYMP) was one of several chemotherapy pathway genes measured in mucinous colorectal cancer and showed no significant difference.

quote: Mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy (MNGIE) is an ultra-rare metabolic autosomal recessive disease, caused by mutations in the nuclear gene TYMP which encodes the enzyme thymidine phosphorylase.
summary: Review of MNGIE caused by TYMP mutations, covering diagnosis, models and experimental therapies; nothing on UC.

quote: Here, we will review two peculiar mitochondrial disorders, ethylmalonic encephalopathy (EE) and mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy (MNGIE), caused by mutations in the ETHE1 and TYMP nuclear genes, respectively.
summary: Review of mitochondrial diseases from toxic compound accumulation, including MNGIE caused by TYMP mutations; no UC content.
